cards.text: In the chapter before this, the prophet Isaiah told Hezekiah, king of Judah, that everything in his palace would one day be carried off to Babylon (Isaiah 39:6). Now this: “Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God. Say it once, that's a message, but say it TWICE, friend, and you'd better lean in.

cards.question: God wants His people comforted. So how should Jerusalem be spoken to? Speak ___ to Jerusalem

cards.text: Then comes what to proclaim to her: her forced labor has been completed. Friend, that's the best text any worker ever gets: “You can clock out.”

cards.question: Jerusalem's forced labor is completed. True or false: her iniquity is still waiting to be dealt with.

cards.text: Her iniquity has been pardoned, and then this: “For she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.” Then a new voice calls out, and it doesn't come with a name tag.

cards.question: This voice calls out to prepare the way for the LORD. Where?

cards.text: And it's not a footpath, either: “make a straight highway for our God in the desert.” That's a road crew getting a job order from GOD, friend, so no pressure.

cards.question: To get that highway ready for God, every valley shall be ___ up
Every valley goes up for God's highway. True or false: every mountain and hill gets raised up too.

cards.text: Uneven ground goes smooth and rugged land becomes a plain. That's me with a rolling pin, friend, except I have NEVER gotten dough this flat.

cards.question: The voice calling out isn't done yet. What does it say will be revealed?
The glory of the LORD will be revealed. Who will see it?

cards.text: And then: “For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.” That's not a maybe, friend, that's DONE.
Now a voice says, “Cry out!” and the prophet asks what he should cry out. Smart, friend, because you never start yelling before you know what you're yelling about.
The answer comes back: “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field.” Okay. Not exactly the pep talk I was hoping for.

cards.question: All flesh is like grass and its glory like flowers. What happens to them when the breath of the LORD blows on them?

answers.text: The grass withers and the flowers fall
The grass grows and the flowers bloom
The grass bends and the flowers sway

cards.text: Then it's said plainly: “indeed, the people are grass.” Friend, I wore down so bad they put me in a junk drawer, so I am NOT arguing.

cards.question: The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands ___

cards.text: Now a new picture: Zion and Jerusalem are both called a herald of good news, and Zion is told to go up on a high mountain. A whole MOUNTAIN, friend, and I get winded hopping my gold base over to the oven.

cards.question: Zion is told to go up on a high mountain. True or false: the herald of good news is told to keep the message quiet.

cards.text: Nope: “Raise your voice loudly, O Jerusalem, herald of good news. Lift it up, do not be afraid!” Mags, my little bell, would've had that whole mountain SHAKING.

cards.question: The herald of good news has a message for the cities of Judah. What is it?

cards.text: Behold, the Lord GOD comes, and He comes with might. Friend, Behold is the Bible's way of saying put the phone DOWN and look up.

cards.question: The Lord GOD comes with might. What does His arm do?

cards.text: His reward is with Him, and His recompense comes right along too. No “ships in 6 to 8 weeks” with this One, friend.

cards.question: Then the picture changes. In the next line, the mighty Lord GOD is like a ___
This shepherd gathers the lambs in His arms. Where does He carry them?
True or false: this shepherd drives the nursing ewes hard so they keep up.

findings.problem: The card spends its second sentence defining the word "Behold" ("Behold is the Bible's way of saying put the phone DOWN and look up"). Explaining a word belongs in the dictionary pop-up. The joke should come from the moment itself, the Lord GOD coming with might.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions a flock, lambs or sheep. The question only says "the picture changes," so the baker has nothing to reason from when choosing between shepherd, gardener and potter. This is luck, not an informed guess. A story card or the question could first say He tends His flock (Isaiah 40:11), or the card could ask a different question.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
